hypotheses.justification: hf is only needed because the current proof goes through ActivationStocks.profiles_stocks_congr, which rewrites with the closed form profileStockOne_eq (requires f p ≠ 0). The statement itself does not need it. Let P = W.profiles and Q = W.controls.profiles W.separated. Their U fields are definitionally equal, their pressure0 fields are equal by rfl, and prefix_f gives P.f q = Q.f q for every q with q.1 ≤ heatJoin. shearA (-2 p.1 radialPartial f p / f p) agrees by prefix_f plus radialPartial_of_left (uses hp, hp.1, hR). shearB (-2 p.1 radialPartial U p / E p) agrees because U is identical and E p = sqrt(2 p.1) f p. ReferenceBounds.p1 = p.1 * (primitive (angularSource h) p / (p.1 * H p)) / L, and H p = 2 p.1 f p agrees at p. angularSource at (x, η) depends on W h (which depends only on U), U, H, radialPartial H and parameterPartial H. H agrees on the open set {q.1 < heatJoin}, so its fderiv agrees there. The integrands of primitive therefore agree for x < heatJoin, i.e. a.e. on the integration interval (0, p.1] ⊆ (-∞, heatJoin], and the primitives are equal (intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae). If f p = 0, the division by zero gives the same junk value on both sides. p2 = p.1 * (primitive axialSource p / p.1 / L) / E p is handled the same way: axialSource uses W, U and its partials (identical), f^2, pressure = pressure0 + primitive f^2 (which agrees on {q.1 ≤ heatJoin}) and parameterPartial pressure (which agrees on the open set {q.1 < heatJoin}). E p agrees. So all four equalities hold without hf.

hX is likewise only used for the closed-form stock lemmas (profileStockOne_eq, profileStockTwo_eq) and for history_of_prefix, inside coordinates_of_prefix. Without it, use the direct argument given for hf. heatJoin_pos gives 0 < heatJoin, so for p.1 ≤ heatJoin the integration interval between 0 and p.1 lies in (-∞, heatJoin] whatever the sign of p.1, and prefix_f holds for every q with q.1 ≤ heatJoin, negative q.1 included. So the integrands of primitive (angularSource h) and primitive (axialSource h) agree a.e. (they can differ only at x = heatJoin), and pressure agrees on {q.1 ≤ heatJoin}. shearA and shearB agree by radialPartial_of_left (uses hp, hp.1, hR) and pointwise agreement of f and E at p. When p.1 = 0 all four quantities are 0 or the same junk value on both sides; when p.1 < 0, E p = sqrt(2 p.1) * f p = 0 on both sides, so p2 and shearB are both 0, and p1 and shearA agree as above. hX and hf can each be removed, and also both together.
